idiom_name: protocol conformance for the legacy API + Codable with explicit coding keys
implementation_notes: A protocol mirroring the legacy contract is implemented by a delegating type over the modern model, while the old wire format is pinned with Codable: CodingKeys carries the frozen names and a hand-written init(from:)/encode(to:) covers what coding keys cannot express (old date formats, decimal text, absent versus null). Codable is the standard library's own encoding abstraction - a type 'that can convert itself into and out of an external representation' - so the shape is declared once and both directions follow. @available(*, deprecated, message:) marks the frozen surface, and a hand-written encoder remains justified when the legacy payload is positional or fixed width, which Codable deliberately does not model.
pitfalls: Synthesized Codable behaviour depends on optionality: an absent key and an explicit null both decode to nil unless init(from:) is written by hand, and old clients often distinguish them.
Swift errors carry types and payloads the legacy client never expected; map to the old codes and messages at the boundary instead of throwing through it.
Renaming the protocol or its members changes the Objective-C/Swift symbol old callers bind to; keep the frozen names even when they violate local style.
